item.title: #3623380: Create OOP replacement for hook_install_tasks and hook_install_tasks_alter
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +372/−21 · php +367/−21 · yml +5
  • Diff: 4f9558d
  • Discussion: #3623380 · 5 contributors · 33 comments
  • Followers: 8
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Installation profiles can now provide their custom install tasks and task alterations through a class instead of hook_install_tasks() and hook_install_tasks_alter() in the .profile file. This removes one of the remaining reasons profiles need a procedural .profile file. The old procedural hooks still work but now trigger deprecation errors.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Procedural hook_install_tasks() and hook_install_tasks_alter() are deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and removed from drupal:13.0.0.
  • New API: New \Drupal\Core\Extension\Install\TasksInterface with getTasks(array &$install_state): array and alter(array &$tasks, array $install_state): void.

Technical details

A profile adds a class in src/Install/Tasks/ (namespace Drupal\PROFILE_NAME\Install\Tasks) that implements \Drupal\Core\Extension\Install\TasksInterface. getTasks(array &$install_state) replaces hook_install_tasks() and alter(array &$tasks, array $install_state) replaces hook_install_tasks_alter(). The class is created through \Drupal::classResolver(), so it can implement ContainerInjectionInterface. Only core services can safely be injected, because this runs before the install is complete.

In install.core.inc, install_tasks() calls the new install_get_tasks() and install_alter_tasks() helpers (both @internal). The procedural PROFILE_install_tasks() and PROFILE_install_tasks_alter() are only called when no OOP implementation supplied tasks (for getTasks) or exists (for alter). When the procedural fallback runs, it triggers an E_USER_DEPRECATED error pointing to https://www.drupal.org/node/3623397. The profile file is still loaded before alter(), so the class can rely on functions defined there.

The directory scan that install_check_class_requirements() used to find Install/Requirements classes was extracted into install_get_fixed_class_name(), which now serves both lookups. It require_onces each PHP file in the directory and keeps the class name of the last file it finds, so keep one class per Install/Tasks directory. The hook docs in core.api.php were updated with the @deprecated notes. Follow-up #3630429 is about changing the doc wording on state versus key value expirable.

Upgrade

Move the procedural hooks into a class, for example src/Install/Tasks/MyProfileTasks.php:

namespace Drupal\myprofile\Install\Tasks;

use Drupal\Core\Extension\Install\TasksInterface;

class MyProfileTasks implements TasksInterface {

  public function getTasks(array &$install_state): array {
    // Return what myprofile_install_tasks() returned.
    return [];
  }

  public function alter(array &$tasks, array $install_state): void {
    // Body of myprofile_install_tasks_alter().
  }

}

Then remove myprofile_install_tasks() and myprofile_install_tasks_alter() from the .profile file. If the class exists, the procedural versions are ignored.

item.title: #3617943: Deprecate DateTimePlus::prepareFormat()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Minor task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +0/−16 · php +0/−16
  • Diff: a6e64ec
  • Discussion: #3617943 · 8 contributors · 29 comments
  • Followers: 10
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 8 contributors

Summary

DateTimePlus::prepareFormat() has been a no-op that returns its argument unchanged since the date formatting optimization in #1844956. It is removed in Drupal 12 (main and 12.0.x) and deprecated in 11.x and 11.5.x. Custom code that subclasses DateTimePlus and overrides or calls this method should stop doing so.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Protected DateTimePlus::prepareFormat() is removed from the main branch (12.x); it was deprecated in 11.5 for removal in 12.0.0.

Technical details

The commit on main deletes the protected function prepareFormat($format) method from core/lib/Drupal/Component/Datetime/DateTimePlus.php. Per the issue, it is unused in core and in contrib. Because the 12.x branch had already had its deprecated code removed before beta, the work was split: the 11.x and 11.5.x commits carry the deprecation (the issue states deprecation in 11.5.0 for removal in 12.0.0, with a change record at node 3619997 linked in the deprecation message), while main and 12.0.x get the removal. The 11.x diff was not part of the fetched commit, so the exact deprecation call was not verified.

Upgrade

If a subclass of DateTimePlus overrides or calls prepareFormat(), remove that code. The method only returned $format unchanged, so pass the format string directly.

item.title: #3621330: Include Bandwidth optimization (aggregation) on Status report page
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +24/−0 · php +24
  • Diff: 659bade
  • Discussion: #3621330 · 6 contributors · 14 comments
  • Followers: 7
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

The Status report page (/admin/reports/status) now shows a "Bandwidth optimization" entry. It reads "Enabled" when both CSS and JavaScript aggregation are on. If either is off, it shows "Disabled" with a warning. This makes it easier to notice that aggregation was turned off by mistake on a live site. The entry links to the Bandwidth optimization section of the Performance settings page.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

A new preprocess_enabled runtime requirement is added in checkRequirements(). It reads css.preprocess and js.preprocess from system.performance config, so config overrides in settings.php are reflected. Severity is RequirementSeverity::Info by default and becomes RequirementSeverity::Warning if either value is falsy. Warning rather than error was chosen because nothing breaks when aggregation is off, it is only sub-optimal. The description includes a "Change bandwidth optimization" link to system.performance_settings with the fragment edit-bandwidth-optimization.

item.title: #3273334: Unable to unselect a multi select exposed filter in ajax view
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +72/−7 · php +58/−5 · js +14/−2
  • Diff: 48f2609
  • Discussion: #3273334 · 13 contributors · 46 comments
  • Followers: 18
  • AI disclosures: 2 of 13 contributors

Summary

In an AJAX-enabled view with a multi-select exposed filter, you can now clear the selection. Previously, if the filter was already in the page URL (for example /admin/content?type[]=page), deselecting the value and pressing Filter re-selected it. The query string parameters for exposed filters are now correctly dropped before the AJAX request, so the submitted form values win. Query parameters in the resulting URLs can appear in a different order.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The bug was in core/modules/views/js/ajax_view.js. When building the AJAX request, the code removes existing exposed filter params from the page's query string, but it only matched input[name="..."] by exact name. select and textarea elements were never matched, and a multi-select named type[] did not match a URL param such as type[0] or type[]. A multi-select with nothing selected submits no value, so the stale URL param was passed through and re-applied.

The fix collects the base names of every [name] element in the exposed form into a Set, stripping any [...] suffix with a stripArraySuffix() helper. It then filters URL params by checking their suffix-stripped name against that set. This removes all exposed form fields from the URL, not only checkboxes and multi-selects, which can change the order of params in generated URLs. The committer noted this is closer to the original intent of the // Remove current exposed filters. comment. Existing FunctionalJavascript tests in the views and admin tests were updated for the new param order (for example title=Page%20Two&type=All&status=All). A new testUnselectMultiSelectExposedFilter covers clearing the selection and the type[0]/type[1] URL form. It was backported to 12.0.x, 11.x and 11.5.x.

item.title: #3635924: Upgrade htmx to 4.0.1
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +118/−98 · js +110/−90 · lock +5/−5 · yml +2/−2 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: b2c92d3
  • Discussion: #3635924 · 3 contributors · 10 comments
  • Followers: 4
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 3 contributors

Summary

Drupal core's bundled htmx JavaScript library is updated from 4.0.0 to 4.0.1. The issue says one fix in this release affects hx-partial, a new htmx 4 feature. The release also fixes other htmx behavior around request handling, triggers, out-of-band swaps and history. Sites and modules that build on core's HTMX support get the fixes automatically, with no code changes. The change was committed to main and 12.0.x.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The htmx library definition in core/core.libraries.yml now points to version 4.0.1, with the license URL updated to match. core/assets/vendor/htmx/htmx.min.js was regenerated, and package.json and yarn.lock pin htmx.org at 4.0.1. The unminified source diff shows these behavior changes:

  • hx-action, the verb attributes (hx-get, hx-post and so on), hx-trigger and hx-validate no longer pick up implicit inheritance from ancestors. #attributeValue gained an allowInheritance argument for this.
  • hx-trigger now accepts every 1s [cond]. The changed modifier is tracked per event target. A new trigger cancels any pending delayed or throttled trigger on the same element. intersect now observes the from: elements.
  • Boosted elements now go through #initializeTriggers.
  • Indicators and disabled elements are tracked on ctx.indicators and ctx.disabledElements. A request that is replaced no longer releases the queue slot of the request that replaced it. AbortError no longer fires htmx:error, except for timeouts. A swap is skipped if the target was removed while the request was in flight.
  • Out-of-band targets are resolved relative to the source element, and swapStyle:selector parsing was changed. The ignoreTitle swap modifier is now honored in more places. A scroll or show target of window or document is handled.
  • History is now stamped with replaceState on the first htmx swap rather than at initialization, and it is updated only after a swap is confirmed.
  • htmx.ajax() rejects with "Target not found" when an explicit target can't be resolved.
  • A named submit button that owns hx-post is treated as the submitter.
  • HTML is parsed with Document.parseHTMLUnsafe(trusted, {}) as a workaround for Chrome 150 to 156 dropping comments.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: November 6, 2026
  • Committed: November 10, 2026 (3 days later)

item.title: #3357616: Remove "Forgot your password?" link on failed login attempt message if user has no access to the user password reset form
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +67/−6 · php +57/−6 · yml +10
  • Diff: abb6fd1
  • Discussion: #3357616 · 11 contributors · 33 comments
  • Followers: 16
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 11 contributors

Summary

Links to the password reset page now appear only when the visitor can actually access it. On sites that disable user.pass (common with external authentication), a failed login now shows "Unrecognized username or password." without the "Forgot your password?" link that previously led to a 403. The same applies to the flood-control blocked messages and the current password hint on the user edit form. Because the strings change, this landed in main only (12.1.0) despite being filed as a bug.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

UserLoginForm::validateFinal() now builds Url::fromRoute('user.pass') once and calls $pass_url->access() before adding the link. Three messages have a no-link variant: the generic failed login error, the user-based flood message (singular and plural via formatPlural()), and the IP-based flood message. The flood variants end with "Try again later." when access is denied. AccountForm::form() applies the same check to the current_pass description, which drops the "Reset your password" link when access is denied. UserLoginForm::validateFinal() runs on form submission, which is not cached, so no cache variation was added (per alexpott's reply to the cache question). Tests add a user_disable_password_reset test module whose RouteSubscriber sets _access: FALSE on user.pass, and UserLoginTest::testFailedLoginMessageWithNoPasswordResetAccess(). Contributors decided against a new configuration option. Controlling the link by route access follows an existing core pattern.

item.title: #3578936: Navigation module and Admin theme should use the same Inter font
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 25 files, +202/−94 · css +182/−74 · yml +20/−12 · php +0/−8
  • Diff: 3875e93
  • Discussion: #3578936 · 8 contributors · 46 comments
  • Followers: 12
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 8 contributors

Summary

Navigation and the Default Admin theme each used to load their own copy of the Inter font, so admin pages with both downloaded it twice (about 557 KB of fonts). Core now ships one shared Inter font, split by character set, and both use it. On a typical English admin page only the Latin subset (about 104 KB) is downloaded and preloaded. The issue's own Slow 4G measurements, which were generated with Claude, show fonts finishing loading about 2.6 seconds sooner. Default Admin moves from Inter v3 to v4, which Navigation already used, so admin headings come out a few percent narrower. Body text is almost unchanged.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Navigation and Default Admin no longer ship their own Inter @font-face CSS or font files; they depend on core/font. Admin typography now uses Inter v4, so headings render slightly narrower.
  • New API: New core/font library (Inter v4 variable, unicode-range subsets, preloaded latin file) and --drupal-font-inter CSS custom property.

Technical details

A new font library in core/core.libraries.yml loads core/misc/fonts/inter.css and preloads misc/fonts/inter-latin.woff2 through the library fonts key. inter.css declares eight @font-face blocks for the Inter family (latin, latin-ext, cyrillic, cyrillic-ext, greek, greek-ext, vietnamese, symbols), each with a unicode-range. Browsers fetch only the subsets needed by the characters on the page. The CSS also defines metric-adjusted fallback faces, Inter Fallback Helvetica Neue and Inter Fallback Arial, using size-adjust, ascent-override, descent-override and line-gap-override to reduce layout shift while Inter loads. :root gets --drupal-font-inter, which lists inter followed by those fallbacks and sans-serif. The --drupal- prefix was added after review to avoid clashing with other themes' variables. An unused --font-inter-size-adjust variable was removed.

Consumers now use the shared pieces. navigation/internal.navigation and default_admin/global-styling list core/font as a dependency, and their own fonts.css/font.css files, fonts: preload entries and (for Default Admin) the v3.19 font file reference are removed. --admin-toolbar-font-family in the Navigation variables and --admin-font-family in Default Admin are both set to var(--drupal-font-inter). The installer test assertion that the preloaded font URL avoids install.php was removed. Performance test expectations (StylesheetBytes) were updated. The change was also backported to 12.0.x, 11.x and 11.5.x.

Upgrade

Themes or modules that bundle their own Inter copy (for example Gin or Mercury, as discussed in the issue) can drop it and depend on the core library:

dependencies:
  - core/font

Then reference the shared stack in CSS:

--admin-font-family: var(--drupal-font-inter);

Custom CSS that depended on Navigation's or Default Admin's fonts.css/font.css files, or on their inter-var.woff2/inter.woff2 file paths, should switch to core/font.

item.title: #3181762: The field name is not displayed in LinkWidget error messages
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +19/−11 · php +19/−11
  • Diff: a65f1b4
  • Discussion: #3181762 · 11 contributors · 35 comments
  • Followers: 13
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 11 contributors

Summary

Validation errors from the Link field widget now name the field they belong to. When an entity form has several Link fields and more than one is invalid, each message identifies its own field instead of showing generic text the user has to hunt down. The wording of the messages changed, so custom tests, translations, or scripts that match the old text need updating.

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: None

Technical details

In LinkWidget::formElement() the URI element now carries a #field_label property copied from the widget element's #title. validateUriElement() uses it as the %field_name placeholder in the invalid internal path messages for the external, internal and generic link types. For example, the generic message is now "The %field_name field must contain a content title, an internal path starting with /, ? or #, or a full external URL including the protocol, such as %link_example." The LINK_INTERNAL message also gained $args, which it previously lacked.

validateTitleNoLink() now reads "The %field_name field: @uri is required when @title is specified.", with %field_name taken from $element['#title']. The old "Enter a content title to select it..." and "External links must be a full URL..." strings are gone. Tests in the link module's LinkFieldTest and a menu_link_content form test were updated to the new strings. The field name pattern follows OptionsWidgetBase.

Upgrade

Update any custom tests or code that assert on the old text, for example:

// Before
'Enter a content title to select it, or enter an internal path starting with /, ? or #.'
// After (internal link type)
'The %field_name field must contain a content title or an internal path starting with /, ? or #.'

The same applies to 'The @uri field is required when the @title field is specified.', which is now 'The %field_name field: @uri is required when @title is specified.'. Translations of the old strings will need re-translating.

item.title: #3615654: Default to using the 'libraries' parameter for CSS aggregates
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 17 files, +52/−31 · php +33/−12 · yml +19/−19
  • Diff: 5a04931
  • Discussion: #3615654 · 5 contributors · 30 comments
  • Followers: 7
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

CSS aggregates now use the exact list of libraries they contain to build their URL, the way JavaScript aggregates already do. Before, a CSS aggregate's URL depended on everything else on the page, so the same content was downloaded again under different query strings on different pages. Now an aggregate that contains the same libraries gets the same URL on every page, which improves browser and CDN cache hits. The number of stylesheet files per page often goes up, but total bytes transferred usually goes down or stays flat. The issue reports some cases about a third smaller, and some Umami pages with fewer files. No configuration is needed.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The change is in CssCollectionGrouper::group() in core/lib/Drupal/Core/Asset/CssCollectionGrouper.php. Previously the libraries parameter was only used for CSS when aggregate_target['css'] was set. Now every preprocessed item that has a library key is recorded in the group's libraries list, so aggregate_target is no longer a precondition. It still controls splitting: TRUE groups by the item's library and a string groups by that name. Group keys still include the item's category, so an aggregate holds only one CSS category (base, theme, component). Libraries that are split across aggregates, for example when one of their files is excluded from aggregation, still fall back to include/exclude. Items without a library key, such as files added in hook_css_alter(), are skipped when recording libraries, and the alter hook is assumed to add them in the same place each time. Include/exclude support is not removed. The thread says that needs per-file weights removed first, and follow-up #3636352 covers documenting that hook_css_alter() and hook_js_alter() should only modify or remove files. The Navigation and CKEditor aggregate_target changes were split out of this issue (#3615642 and #3622766). Most of the diff is updated performance test expectations (StylesheetCount and StylesheetBytes) and CssCollectionGrouperUnitTest fixtures, which now carry category and library keys.

Upgrade

Custom or contrib code that adds CSS files in hook_css_alter() without a library key still works. Those files are not included in the libraries list. Attaching them to a real library is more robust.

item.title: #3633459: Update CKEditor to 49.1.0
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 83 files, +872/−826 · lock +618/−643 · jsdoc +114/−80 · js +73/−73 · yml +28/−28 · css +23/−1 · php +15 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: acfffb4
  • Discussion: #3633459 · 5 contributors · 37 comments
  • Followers: 8
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Drupal core's bundled CKEditor 5 is updated from 48.5.1 to 49.1.0. The upstream release is a security update that the issue says does not affect Drupal core. Editors will see two small visual changes: the editor now stops growing 15px earlier, and balloon tooltips in the Admin theme keep readable text in light mode. Sites with custom CKEditor 5 plugins or CSS that overrides CKEditor variables should retest against v49.

Impact

Affects front-end developers and site owners.

  • Requirements: Bundled CKEditor 5 updated from 48.5.1 to 49.1.0 in core/core.libraries.yml and core/package.json.
  • Theme change: default_admin CKEditor 5 CSS now sets .ck.ck-balloon-panel background from --ck-balloon-panel-background-color. The editor max-height offset changed from 20px to 35px.

Technical details

The vendored build under core/assets/vendor/ckeditor5 is regenerated, including all translation files. The version and license URL entries in core/core.libraries.yml and the ckeditor5 dependency in core/package.json are bumped to 49.1.0. The update was committed to main and 12.0.x. The issue notes that 11.x through 10.6.x stay on a security fork of 47.6 and get no update.

v49 changed how the balloon panel background is resolved. .ck.ck-balloon-panel now uses background: var(--ck-color-panel-background, var(--ck-balloon-panel-background-color)), and the more specific .ck.ck-balloon-panel.ck-tooltip rule that previously set --ck-color-panel-background was removed. The default_admin theme sets --ck-color-panel-background to a light/dark dependent value, so in light mode tooltips rendered white text on a white background. The fix adds .ck.ck-balloon-panel { background: var(--ck-balloon-panel-background-color); } to the default_admin CKEditor 5 CSS (both the source .pcss.css and the compiled CSS). Tooltips are readable again but do not follow light or dark mode. That is deferred to follow-up #3634547.

New CKEditor styles added a top margin that pushed the editor past the viewport in CKEditor5HeightTest. The max-height rule in the ckeditor5 editor CSS now subtracts 35px instead of 20px. The ckeditor5.types.jsdoc build output and the performance test script byte counts were also updated.

Two JS tests (testLinkability and the media test that edits source) now click .ck-widget__type-around__button_after and call assertBalloonClosed(). This closes the media balloon that otherwise covers the Source button. One test also presses Source again to return to rich text editing so the source changes reach the CKEditor data model. The thread says this is only needed in the test, not in manual use.

Upgrade

Sites or contrib themes that override --ck-color-panel-background and want it to apply to tooltips should check balloon tooltips against v49. default_admin handled it this way:

.ck.ck-balloon-panel {
  background: var(--ck-balloon-panel-background-color);
}

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: October 27, 2026
  • Committed: November 8, 2026 (12 days later)

Key contributors

  • xjm (xjm)
  • godotislate
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)

Collaboration

godotislate did the update in the MR. When the JS tests failed, they traced the invisible light-mode tooltips to a CSS backwards-compatibility change in CKEditor v49 and wrote the default_admin fix. They also traced the CKEditor5HeightTest failure to the max-height rule from #3273755. xjm worked out that this test checks auto-expansion of the editor and noticed that 49.1.0 had been released, so the MR was moved from 49.0.1 to 49.1.0.

item.title: #3619733: Deprecate .module file extension
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 42 files, +267/−24 · php +257/−24 · yml +10
  • Diff: 3fb1c69
  • Discussion: #3619733 · 10 contributors · 63 comments
  • Followers: 17
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 10 contributors

Summary

Procedural .module files are now deprecated, and so are .profile files. Drupal emits one deprecation notice per file, naming the file. This tells module and profile maintainers to move any remaining code into classes: hooks into hook classes, other functions into services or other classes. The deprecation applies to the files, not to modules as an extension type. The notice is only emitted on main and 12.0.x. It was not backported to 11.5.x, although the deprecation text says 11.5.0 and the change record (https://www.drupal.org/node/3619765) is published. Core's own .module files are converted. The ones that still hold deprecated legacy functions are marked with the attribute to stay quiet.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Code in .module and .profile files is deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and must be converted before drupal:13.0.0. The deprecation notice is emitted only on main and 12.0.x, not on 11.x.
  • New API: #[ExtensionFileIsConverted] is now also honoured in .module and .profile files. Put it on the first function in the file to suppress the deprecation notice.

Technical details

HookCollectorPass already scanned .module and .profile files for procedural hook implementations. It now records every such file it finds in a new deprecatedFiles property. In writeToContainer() it emits Code in {name}.{ext} is deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and must be converted before drupal:13.0.0. Use classes instead. See https://www.drupal.org/node/3619765.

A file is removed from that list, so no notice is emitted, in two cases. First, if a function in it carries #[ExtensionFileIsConverted]. Second, if every function in it carries #[LegacyHook] or #[LegacyRequirementsHook] (so a file holding only legacy hook wrappers produces no notice). The result is cached under a new @skip_extension_file_deprecation key.

The procedural scan used to be skipped entirely when $skip_procedural was set or #[ProceduralHookScanStop] was hit. Deprecation detection needs to see every function in the file, so the scan now always runs. When either skip condition applies, it only stops adding hooks to the hook map and keeps looking for non-legacy functions. The cached structure changed from a flat list to ['hooks' => [...], '@skip_extension_file_deprecation' => TRUE]. The file-cache keys were bumped (hook_implementations:1, procedural_hook_implementations:1:...) so old entries are not reused.

The attribute can only target a function. A .module file that contains no functions therefore needs a dummy function to carry it, as discussed in the thread. The .theme collector got the same treatment and its message text was aligned with the module wording (Code in ... is deprecated ... must be converted before drupal:13.0.0). Core .module files that still hold deprecated legacy functions (for example text_summary(), filter_formats(), views_add_contextual_links()) got #[ExtensionFileIsConverted]. Legacy test modules and profiles that intentionally keep procedural code now expect the deprecation in their tests. The related theme change is #3581218.

Upgrade

To silence the notice while a .module file must remain (for example to support older core), add the attribute to the first function in the file, as core did:

use Drupal\Core\Hook\Attribute\ExtensionFileIsConverted;

#[ExtensionFileIsConverted]
function text_summary($text, $format = NULL, $size = NULL) {

Per the attribute docs, use it only for legacy support. If your minimum supported core is 11.3.0 or later, convert the file's contents to classes and remove the .module file. See https://www.drupal.org/node/3619765.

item.title: #3278431: [November 2026] Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion for existing code
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 910 files, +5738/−16962 · php +5738/−16962
  • Diff: 780eb17
  • Discussion: #3278431 · 19 contributors · 104 comments
  • Followers: 62
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 19 contributors

Summary

Drupal core (main, also cherry-picked to 12.0.x) now uses PHP 8 constructor property promotion across existing code. Injected services and values are declared once in the constructor signature (protected FooInterface $foo,) instead of as separate property declarations plus assignments. Site owners have nothing to do. The change affects module developers only if they call core constructors with named arguments, because some parameter names changed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Many core constructor parameters were renamed from snake_case to camelCase to match their promoted properties (e.g. $csrf_token to $csrfToken), which only breaks callers using named arguments; see change record 3635267.

Technical details

The change was produced by running Rector's ClassPropertyAssignToConstructorPromotionRector with INLINE_PUBLIC enabled, so untyped public and protected properties are also promoted. The Rector output was then run through PHP CS Fixer and phpcbf to put each promoted constructor on multiple lines with a trailing comma. A few tests that assert on line numbers were fixed by hand, and the PHPStan baseline was regenerated. The shipped diff covers hundreds of files, including core/lib/Drupal/Component, core/lib/Drupal/Core and the composer scaffold and package code. Visible examples are AccessManager, the Ajax commands, the action plugins and the scaffold operations such as AppendOp.

Property names, visibility and property types do not change. Existing untyped properties stay untyped, for example protected $reason. What changes is that constructor parameters which were snake_case now take the camelCase property name. For example $csrf_token becomes $csrfToken in CsrfAccessCheck and $request_stack becomes $requestStack in Time. Where the property and parameter already matched, nothing is renamed. The @var property docblocks were dropped with the properties. The constructor @param docblocks were kept, with the parameter names updated. Removing those docblocks is tracked separately in #3565152. Follow-ups for adding type declarations and readonly to promoted parameters are in #3635274.

Participants decided not to support named arguments for constructors, so the renames were not given a deprecation layer. Where a constructor mixed promoted and plain parameters, such as plugin constructors that call parent::__construct(), only the matching parameters were promoted. The rest are still assigned in the body.

Upgrade

Only code that calls core constructors with named arguments is affected. Switch to the new camelCase parameter names, or use positional arguments. For example, CsrfAccessCheck:

// Before
new CsrfAccessCheck(csrf_token: $token);
// After
new CsrfAccessCheck(csrfToken: $token);

Subclasses that override a constructor and call parent::__construct() positionally are unaffected.

item.description:

Summary

Core's system library definitions no longer use per-file CSS weights. The five utility stylesheets in system/base (align, container-inline, clearfix, hidden, js) now sit in the base CSS group, which loads before component, so they still load early. Weights were also dropped from other system libraries. One fewer stylesheet file is aggregated in the standard performance test. Themes or modules that override or remove these files under the component group keep working, but with a deprecation message, until they switch to base. This is part of the effort to deprecate per-file weight in the libraries API (#3467488).

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: The system/base CSS files align, container-inline, clearfix, hidden and js (css/components/*.module.css) moved from the component group to the base group. Theme libraries-override entries should use base instead of component.
  • Deprecation: The old system/base component locations of those five CSS files are deprecated via moved_files (deprecation_version 11.5.0, removed_version 13.0.0).

Technical details

In core/modules/system/system.libraries.yml, system/base previously listed its CSS under component with weight: -10 so it loaded early. It now lists them under base with no weight. A moved_files entry maps each old component path to the same file under base. It has deprecation_version: 11.5.0, removed_version: 13.0.0 and a link to this issue. Existing overrides keyed on the old location are therefore still resolved, and they trigger deprecation messages.

The remaining weight: -10 entries were removed from system/maintenance (kept in the theme group), system/status.report (kept in component) and drupal.system.admin_compact (kept in theme). The issue thread says the maintenance CSS stays in theme because theme files always load after module files, and the maintenance page styling is hard-coded in preprocessMaintenancePage(). A follow-up, #3623221, was opened to deprecate the system.maintenance library.

Test fixtures were updated to match: a test module's libraryInfoAlter() now adds its CSS under base, and a libraries-override fixture for system/base now targets base for css/components/js.module.css. Performance test expectations were also changed for the stylesheet count. The change was committed to main and 12.0.x, and also backported to 11.x and 11.5.x.

Upgrade

If a theme overrides or removes these files in system/base, change the group key from component to base:

libraries-override:
  system/base:
    css:
      base:
        css/components/js.module.css: false

Using the old component key still works until 13.0.0, but it triggers a deprecation message.

item.title: #3425412: [November 2026] Bump PHPStan rule level to 3
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +67/−4 · lock +63/−1 · json +2 · txt +1 · dist +1/−3
  • Diff: 56f6338
  • Discussion: #3425412 · 18 contributors · 119 comments
  • Followers: 30
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 18 contributors

Summary

Drupal core's static analysis now runs at PHPStan rule level 3 instead of level 1. Levels 2 and 3 add checks for unknown methods on any expression, PHPDoc validation, return types and types assigned to properties. Existing violations were added to the baseline file, so core's own checks keep passing. New code that violates these rules now fails the PHPStan job. Open merge requests that touch the baseline or add such violations will probably need a rebase and fixes. The change was committed to main and backported to 12.0.x.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: New dev dependency jangregor/phpstan-prophecy (^2.2, locked at 2.3.0) in core's composer.json require-dev.

Technical details

core/phpstan.neon.dist changes level: 1 to level: 3. It also drops the explicit PHPStan\Rules\Classes\AccessPrivateConstantThroughStaticRule, whose comment said it could go once the level reached 2. The explicit return-typehint rules stay, since their comment says they can go at level 6. checkFunctionArgumentTypes: true was already set, so the argument type checks that level 5 mainly adds were already active.

jangregor/phpstan-prophecy is added to require-dev (composer.json and the core composer.json) and composer.lock is updated. It lets PHPStan resolve Prophecy mocks to the types they mock. The issue says this avoids roughly 2k false positives in the baseline. jangregor is added to the cspell dictionary. The regenerated core/.phpstan-baseline.php was not in the diff I read. In the thread, the baseline at level 3 was measured at about 11,000 entries and 3.3 MB, against 1.7 MB at level 1.

The thread also compared levels 4 to 9. Level 5 adds little over level 4 because argument type checking is already on, and level 4 would add about 2,500 errors that can be cleaned up in minor releases. The release managers chose level 3. Their reasoning was that tightening typing contracts is a major-only change.

Upgrade

Contrib and core developers who run core's PHPStan config should rebase open branches and regenerate the baseline if it conflicts. The CI job produces the regenerated baseline as a downloadable artifact. Code touched in a branch may now report level 2 and 3 errors. The new dev dependency is installed with:

composer require --dev jangregor/phpstan-prophecy

Summary

The error summary that Inline Form Errors shows at the top of a form, such as "3 errors have been found:" followed by links to the fields, now renders through a real Twig template. Before, the module built it as a raw render array, so themes had nothing to override. Themes and sites can now customize its markup, for example to match a base theme's alert styling, and can target a single form. The default output is almost the same as before. The only visible change is a <span> around the count text.

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: The "N errors have been found:" summary now renders through a template, and the count text is wrapped in a new <span>.
  • New API: New inline_form_errors_summary theme hook with inline_form_errors_summary.html.twig and an inline_form_errors_summary__FORM_ID suggestion.

Technical details

FormErrorHandler::displayErrorMessages() used to build the summary from a #markup plural string plus an item_list render array. It now builds one render array with #theme => 'inline_form_errors_summary', #error_links and #form_id (taken from $form['#form_id']), then passes it to renderInIsolation() and addError(). Each link is wrapped as ['value' => <link renderable>] so the list is fed to item-list.html.twig as items.

InlineFormErrorsThemeHooks gains a hook_theme() implementation declaring the error_links and form_id variables. It also gains a hook_theme_suggestions_inline_form_errors_summary() implementation that adds inline_form_errors_summary__FORM_ID when a form ID is present. The new inline_form_errors_summary.html.twig uses {% trans %} with plural handling for the count, wraps the count text in a <span>, and includes item-list.html.twig with context: {list_style: 'comma-list'}.

FormErrorHandlerTest was refactored because the render array shape changed, and a test was added that checks the #theme, #form_id and #error_links values. PathAliasTest assertions were split into two statusMessageContains() calls because the span changes the whitespace around the text. Field-level inline error markup and the fieldset case from the original report were not touched. Only the summary got a template.

Summary

The "Convert line breaks into HTML (i.e. <br> and <p>)" text filter now emits HTML5 style <br> for single line breaks instead of the XHTML style <br />. Browsers render both the same, but any custom test, snapshot or string match that expects the literal <br /> from this filter will need updating. It was committed to main and backported to 12.0.x, because Drupal 12 should be fully HTML5 and the maintainer judged it low risk.

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Text run through the "Convert line breaks into HTML" filter (FilterAutoP) now contains <br> instead of <br /> in rendered output.

Technical details

The line-break logic lives in FilterAutoP::process() (the former _filter_autop()). The "make line breaks" regexes now insert and look for <br>: (?<!<br>)\s*\n is replaced with <br>\n, and the two cleanup regexes around block-level tags and p|li|div|dl|dd|dt|th|pre|td|ul|ol match <br>. The earlier step that collapses two consecutive breaks into a paragraph break was widened to <br ?/?>\s*<br ?/?>, so input that already contains <br>, <br/> or <br /> is still collapsed. Only the output side is switched to <br>.

The merged change touches FilterAutoP and FilterKernelTest only. The test expectations in testLineBreakFilter() were updated to <br>. In testHtmlCorrectorFilter() only the assertion message changed: Html::normalize('<br></br>') still yields <br><br>, which is why the description now says it is transformed into two br tags. Earlier review (catch, wim leers) noted that Html::normalize() and the filter system already emit HTML5 serialization since #2441811, which is why this filter was one of the remaining places still producing <br />. The parent effort is #1388926. A reviewer (nod_) asked whether the old <br /> forms could still occur, for example from CKEditor 4 configuration, which is why the first regex still accepts all three spellings.

item.title: #2735997: Decimal separator and precision settings unavailable when aggregating decimal fields
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +216/−7 · php +169/−7 · yml +47
  • Diff: cf863a1
  • Discussion: #2735997 · 30 contributors · 122 comments
  • Followers: 45

Summary

When a View uses aggregation (Sum, Average and similar) on a Decimal or Float field, the field settings now include the Round, Precision and Decimal point options. Before, those options were missing for aggregated decimal fields, so you could not control decimal places or the decimal separator in the output. Base decimal fields on entity types also now get numeric filter and contextual filter (argument) handlers instead of the generic standard ones. An earlier attempt at this issue was reverted after it broke COUNT and date aggregation output. This version leaves the aggregation handler override alone.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Views field definitions for decimal and float fields now carry 'float' => TRUE, which exposes precision and decimal point settings on aggregated fields.

Technical details

When aggregation is on, Sql::getAggregationInfo() swaps in the numeric field handler for functions like Sum and Average. NumericField::buildOptionsForm() only shows precision and decimal point settings when the handler definition contains float => TRUE, and Views data never set that flag for decimal or float fields. The fix sets $data[...]['field']['float'] = TRUE in two places. FieldViewsDataProvider::defaultFieldImplementation() does it for configurable fields whose schema column type is float or numeric, which covers the decimal field type. EntityViewsData::mapSingleFieldViewsData() does it for base fields.

In EntityViewsData, the numeric column type was previously unhandled and fell into the default branch. It is now grouped with float, double and decimal, so base decimal fields get the numeric argument and filter plugins. The common field and sort ids were hoisted above the column-type switch. Integer columns keep the numeric argument and filter but get no float flag.

This is the second attempt. The first commit removed the field => numeric override from getAggregationInfo(), which caused regressions (see #3517853, #3518896) and was reverted. The form submit exception found along the way was split to #3613882. Tests added: kernel tests for FieldViewsDataProvider and EntityViewsData, a QueryGroupByTest::testAggregateDecimalOutput() check that a summed value of 5.789 renders as 5,79, and a FieldUITest functional test. The commit landed on main and 12.0.x, and was backported to 11.x and 11.5.x.

Collaboration

The first fix removed the numeric handler override from getAggregationInfo(). It was committed, then reverted after regressions were reported. acbramley reported the COUNT and date output regressions, argued that the override is required for aggregated output, and prepared the revert MR. joelpittet then reworked the MR to keep the override and set the float flag in the Views data instead. acbramley retested the change on the affected client site and asked for test coverage of the decimal output, which the MR then gained.
